title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance

task.value: An LLM-powered multi-agent framework with layered memory and distinct trader characters for stock and fund trading decisions.
task.quote: We assert that this framework is well-suited for stock and fund trading, where the extraction of highly relevant insights from hierarchical financial data is imperative to inform trading decisions.

architecture.value: Multiple LLM agents, each with short/middle/long-term memory layers ranked by recency, relevancy and importance; daily immediate and extended reflections; risk-preference characters; inter-agent debate on shared stocks; FAISS vector store.
architecture.quote: This represents a pioneering multi-agent trading system that integrates memory streams and debate mechanisms, anchored on LLMs. Building on Park et al.’s weighted memory mechanisms, our system innovatively categorizes the agent’s memories into short-term, middle-term, and long-term layers

data.value: Multi-modal financial data Aug 15, 2020 to Aug 15, 2023: Databento stock prices, Alpaca News API, ARK daily holdings records, ARK Invest video transcriptions via Whisper.
data.quote: These datasets were sourced from financial databases and APIs, exemplified by the Databento Stock Price Database, Alpaca News API, publicly available daily holdings history records from ARK, etc.

window.value: Planned: training Aug 15, 2020 to Feb 15, 2023; testing until Aug 15, 2023.
window.quote: The training phase will utilize data spanning from August 15, 2020, to February 15, 2023, while the testing phase will extend until August 15, 2023.

models.value: GPT3.5 turbo used as backbone for prompt design; CodeLlama 34B planned for comparison.
models.quote: We’ve crafted efficient LLM prompts using GPT3.5 turbo as the backbone.

baselines.value: Planned comparisons: GPT3.5 turbo versus CodeLlama 34B backbones, and multi-agent reinforcement learning.
baselines.quote: This will involve comparisons within LLMs, such as GPT3.5 turbo versus CodeLlama 34B, and against models like multi-agent reinforcement learning.

leakage_controls.value: During testing, agents do not use the fund firm's trading records, relying only on daily stock prices as market facts.
leakage_controls.quote: During testing, agents operate without the guidance of trading records from the representative fund firm, relying solely on daily stock prices as market facts.

limitations.value: Work is at an early stage: only prompt design done; ablation studies and performance evaluation are future work.
limitations.quote: With our established prompt template, we’re poised to undertake ablation studies to assess the trading efficacy of agent systems based on various backbone models.
